entries.name: Precision
entries.notes: SHIPPED — id and kindId kept verbatim per naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies (g.precision existingFamilies); kebab-case is a no-op here since `precision` has no underscore. `channel: combat.accuracy.{variant}` element-expansion is genuine, not decorative: DerivedStatChannels.cs declares CombatAccuracyOmni/Fire/Ice/Air/Earth/Light/Dark as real per-element channels, so `variants: {generate: elements+omni}` follows the exemplar's stat.derived pattern (the variant lives in the channel string) rather than the resource.delta `params.element` pattern g.on-hit uses — stat.derived's ParamSchema declares only channel/op/amount (AtomKindRegistry.cs:95-97), with no `element` param to hold it. UNITS: this channel is genuinely sigmoid resolver points (AccuracyScale = 100.0), confirmed by atom-layer-handoff.md §1 and CombatPolicies.cs:9-14 — bands.v1.json's `sigmoidDerivedChannel` group, not `flatDerivedChannel`. RUNTIME HONESTY: stat.derived is quarantined None/None/None (D6) until E12's BattleStatComposer; these rows import and bind nowhere today, a known scheduled gap, not a reason to author the family differently. `roles` is the `precis` column of ssot-affixes.md §4.3's role x group matrix (cells with weight > 0 only), translated from the stale 12-role table the way g.on-hit's sibling did: sense-utility->sense, manipulator-offense->manipulator, jewel-major stays, jewel-minor->both jewel-minor-a and jewel-minor-b, head-protective->head-guard, armament-primary stays. armament-secondary, core-protective, mantle-utility, footing and girdle-resource all carry weight 0 for `precis` and are correctly absent; ward-array, infusion and retinue have no cell in the stale matrix at all and are conservatively excluded rather than guessed at. The commander-only `standard` role is excluded on principle — core.v1.json's `commanderOnly` is a separate list from the 15 body roles, bound at `match` scope from its own 100‰ budget — even though `standard`'s own `precis` weight happens to be non-zero; that is a different mechanism, not a body-role appetite.

entries.name: Keen Edge
entries.notes: SHIPPED — id kebab-cased from `keen_edge` per atom-family-library.md's naming note. Same channel-embedded-variant pattern as `precision` above (`combat.crit.rate.{variant}`, CombatCritRateOmni/Fire/Ice/Air/Earth/Light/Dark all real per DerivedStatChannels.cs), same `sigmoidDerivedChannel` unit family, same `roles` list — the role x group matrix has one row per role per GROUP, not per family, so every entry in this file repeats the same seven roles verbatim; that repetition is correct, not copy-paste sloppiness.

entries.name: Cruelty
entries.notes: SHIPPED — id kept verbatim, already kebab-case. `combat.crit.damage.{variant}` (CombatCritDamageOmni/Fire/Ice/Air/Earth/Light/Dark, DerivedStatChannels.cs), same group, same seven roles as its two siblings above. This closes the three-channel Flat coverage this group ships today: accuracy (`precision`), crit rate (`keen_edge`), crit damage (`cruelty`).

entries.name: Calibrated Sightline
entries.displayTemplate: sets {element} accuracy to {value}, ignoring other modifiers
entries.notes: NEW family minted on this group's reserved `prec` stem (naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies), word `fixation` — short and mechanical, not a flavour word. `op: Replace` rather than a second `Flat`: bands.v1.json's `sigmoidDerivedChannel` unit line documents a Flat-shaped magnitude table only for this channel-family group, unlike `flatDerivedChannel`'s explicit op-by-op branching that gives `Increased` a defined per-mille resolution — minting an `Increased` sibling here would invent a scaling formula this registry does not state. A second `Flat` family on the same channel would also just be a duplicate mechanic, since op is the only thing distinguishing two families sharing one channel (the `elemental_power`/`elpw-amplify` precedent). `Replace` sidesteps both problems: AtomKindRegistry's derived-op enum documents Replace/Flag as structural, no-tier-band-magnitude ops wherever they are used, not scoped to one channel-family group, so nothing here is undefined. `powerBand` on this entry therefore drives item-level and rarity tier-gating only, never a scaled magnitude — a calibrated, fixed accuracy reading that overrides whatever the additive/Increased pipeline would otherwise have produced.

entries.name: Foregone Verdict
entries.displayTemplate: sets {element} critical rate to {value}, ignoring other modifiers
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `prec`, word `verdict`. Same structural `Replace` reasoning as `prec-fixation` above, applied to `combat.crit.rate.{variant}` instead of accuracy — a fixed crit-rate reading, useful either as a floor on an otherwise crit-starved build or a ceiling on a heavily stacked one, either way sitting outside the additive/Increased pipeline entirely rather than adding to it.

entries.name: Harvest Reckoning
entries.displayTemplate: sets {element} critical damage to {value}, ignoring other modifiers
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `prec`, word `reckoning`. Same structural `Replace` reasoning again, on `combat.crit.damage.{variant}` — the third and last channel this group owns, closing out Flat-plus-Replace coverage for all three: accuracy (`precision` / `prec-fixation`), crit rate (`keen_edge` / `prec-verdict`), crit damage (`cruelty` / `prec-reckoning`).

entries.name: Unerring Eye
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `prec`, word `truesight`. `op: Flag` on `combat.accuracy.{variant}` — a boolean toggle rather than a graded reading, mechanically distinct from both `precision` (adds resolver points) and `prec-fixation` (sets a fixed point value): this family either applies or it does not, so `displayTemplate` deliberately carries no `{value}` placeholder, the same way `volley`'s spawn.entity sibling in g.on-hit carries no element param when it has nothing to vary. `powerBand: high` reflects a design judgement, not a scaling claim (Flag is structural per `prec-fixation`'s note): a guaranteed-hit effect is strong enough that it should gate to a later item-level tier window rather than show up on an early roll.
